claims.text: The target material is a quaternary equiatomic single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy.
The target alloy has a random atomic distribution.
The target alloy has high lattice distortion.
Equiatomic multicomponent alloys have high mixing entropy.
At cryogenic temperatures, plasticity transitions from dislocation glide to deformation twinning or deformation-induced amorphization.
Pronounced deformation nanotwinning occurs in CoCrFeMnNi under cryogenic deformation.
Deformation-induced amorphization occurs in CrMnFeCoNi.
Short-range order clusters are present in the target quaternary alloy.
Short-range order increases resistance to dislocation glide and contributes to strengthening.
Nanotwins or amorphous regions act as barriers to dislocation glide.
High lattice friction and short-range order impede dislocation glide at low temperature.
Increasing strain rate reduces the time available for thermally activated dislocation motion.
A shift to twinning or amorphization makes yield strength insensitive to further strain-rate increases.
The strain-rate insensitivity occurs because the activation volume of the dominant mechanism approaches zero.
At 77 K and sufficiently high strain rates, the strain-rate sensitivity of yield strength reaches a plateau.
At room temperature, yield strength increases linearly with strain rate because dislocation glide is the primary yielding mechanism.
The alloy reaches its maximum yield strength and ductility at 77 K because of pronounced nanotwinning.
Standard FCC alloys show a monotonic increase in yield strength with strain rate through thermally activated dislocation glide.
BCC phases or ordered B2 precipitates have strengthening mechanisms different from those of a single-phase FCC alloy.
Ordered B2 phases can increase yield strength through load transfer.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^1 s^-1, a span of five orders of magnitude, while the conditions field calls this a four-order-of-magnitude span.
The target is repeatedly described as quaternary, but CrMnFeCoNi/CoCrFeMnNi—the principal comparator used for the mechanism—is a five-element quinary system rather than a quaternary system.
